diagnostic_evidence.quote: by choosing a test function whose support does not contain any $\bm{x}_i$, one can see that the image set of $T$ is contained in $\{\bm{x}_i\}_i$

issues.failure_explanation: The condition $T\#\mathrm{Leb}=\hat\mu$ is insensitive to modifications of $T$ on Lebesgue-null sets, so it only implies that $T$ takes values in $\{\bm{x}_i\}$ almost everywhere, not that the image set of $T$ is contained in $\{\bm{x}_i\}$ as claimed. Any map that sends a null set outside $\{\bm{x}_i\}$ (and otherwise realizes the volumes) satisfies $T\#\mathrm{Leb}=\hat\mu$ but is not a partition map in the sense defined ($T:\Omega\to\{\bm{x}_i\}$). The test-function argument only yields $\int\phi(T(x))dx=0$, i.e. $\phi\circ T=0$ a.e.

failure_location.quote: Then a map $T:\Omega\to\Omega$ is a partition map if and only if $T\#\mathrm{Leb} = \hat{\mu}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the equivalence up to Lebesgue-null sets (or define partition maps a.e.) and adjust the proof accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if and only if' is false as stated in the reverse direction; the subsequent use of the equivalence to reformulate the Monge problem is unaffected in substance since optimal transport is insensitive to null sets.
issues.title: Push-forward characterization of partition maps only holds up to null sets
issues.why_classification: A local, routine restatement fixes the lemma with no loss to any downstream claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure
No particular constraint is imposed on the centroids $\bm{x}_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The only hypothesis is $c_i\in C^{1,1}(\Omega)$. This does not exclude that $c_i-c_j$ is constant on a set of positive Lebesgue measure (e.g. two particles at the same position with the same cost, or costs with plateaus, as allowed since no constraint is imposed on centroids). In such cases the sets $\{c_i-w_i\le c_j-w_j\}$ overlap on positive measure, the volume equations \eqref{eq:laguerrevolume} cannot be satisfied by Laguerre cells alone, and the Monge problem has infinitely many solutions, so uniqueness and the null-intersection claim fail. The cited references require a nondegeneracy (twist-type) condition that is absent here.

failure_location.quote: Then the Monge problem \eqref{eq:Monge} has a unique solution $T$ given by

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that for all $i\ne j$ and all constants $t$, the level set $\{c_i-c_j=t\}$ is Lebesgue-null (or distinct seeds with a twist condition).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated is false in degenerate configurations; generic cost families used in the paper satisfy the missing condition, so applications are unaffected.
issues.title: Uniqueness/null-intersection claims in the semi-discrete theorem need a nondegeneracy hypothesis on the costs
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local nondegeneracy condition restores the statement with no loss of scope for the paper's applications.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: return as output the unique vector of optimal values for the Kantorovitch potentials $(w_1, \dots, w_N)$

issues.failure_explanation: The Laguerre cells \eqref{eq:Laguerre} depend only on differences $w_i-w_j$, so $(w_1+t,\dots,w_N+t)$ yields the same cells and volumes for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$. The vector of potentials is therefore never unique; only its equivalence class modulo constants is. The theorem and the description of solvers assert strict uniqueness.

failure_location.quote: the weights $w_i\in \mathbb{R}$, called Kantorovich potentials, are uniquely defined such that for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State uniqueness up to an additive constant, or impose a normalization such as $\sum_i w_i=0$.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness statement is false as written; nothing else depends on strict uniqueness (only cells matter).
issues.title: Kantorovich potentials are only unique up to an additive constant
issues.why_classification: A one-line normalization fixes the statement with no mathematical loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
is of the form 
\[\mathscr{S}(w) = \{\bm{x}\in\Omega,\,\, c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) \leq w\},\]
for some $w>0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Monotonicity and the limits do not give an intermediate value: $U$ jumps at any $w$ for which $|\{c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)=w\}|>0$, and then no $w^*$ with $U(w^*)=v_i$ need exist. For a cost constant on a region of positive measure the minimizer of $\mathcal I$ under the volume constraint is a proper subset of a plateau and is not a level set, so the lemma's conclusion is false without a hypothesis that all level sets of $c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)$ are Lebesgue-null (also $U(0)=0$ presupposes $|\{c=0\}|=0$). Uniqueness of $w^*$ likewise needs strict monotonicity, though it is not used.

failure_location.quote: since the function $U : w \mapsto |\mathscr{S}(w)|$ is non-decreasing, $U(0)=0$ and $U(w)\to1$ as $w\to+\infty$ there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that level sets of $c(\cdot,\bm{x}_i)$ have zero Lebesgue measure (so $U$ is continuous), and drop 'unique'.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma and the assertion that individual shapes are always level sets fail for costs with plateaus; the paper's actual cost families (power/polar costs) satisfy the needed condition.
issues.title: Existence of the level-set threshold $w^*$ requires continuity of $U$ (null level sets), not established
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis repairs the lemma; all uses in the paper remain valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which corresponds to lowering the potential and thus allowing deformations in the directions of large nonnegative gradients
This corresponds to a larger cost in the direction of larger gradient but even larger for negative gradient.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\varphi=-\log c$ one has $c=e^{-\varphi}$, so lowering $\varphi$ increases the cost. The perturbation $f=-\delta_+$ therefore raises the cost in directions of positive gradient and penalizes (not allows) deformation toward the chemoattractant, and $f=\delta_-^2+\delta_+$ lowers the cost where the gradient is negative. Both described mechanisms (elongation toward the gradient, fan orthogonal to it, chemotactic migration) presuppose that $\varphi$ increases with $c$, i.e. $\varphi=\log c$; the definition and the interpretations are mutually inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\varphi=-\log c$ by $\varphi=\log c$ (or flip the sign of $f$ in both perturbations) so that the definitions match the described mechanism.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the chemotaxis construction would produce the opposite deformation bias to the one described; the reported behavior corresponds to the opposite sign convention.
issues.title: Sign of the logarithmic potential contradicts the stated effect of the chemotactic perturbations
issues.why_classification: A single sign change makes the construction consistent with all stated conclusions; no result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The caption asserts that internalization occurs under $\gamma_{bo}<\gamma_{bw}-\gamma_{ow}$, but with the listed parameters $\gamma_{bw}-\gamma_{ow}=7-30=-23<5=\gamma_{bo}$, so the stated regime condition is not satisfied by the very simulation offered as its illustration. The condition consistent with the parameters and with internalization of the orange population (orange avoiding the medium) is $\gamma_{bo}<\gamma_{ow}-\gamma_{bw}$, i.e. $\gamma_{ow}>\gamma_{bo}+\gamma_{bw}$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated regime criterion for internalization is wrong as written; the numerical experiment itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Stated internalization condition is violated by the parameters used
issues.why_classification: Correcting the inequality is local and preserves the reported phenomenon and parameters.
